# Circuit Tracer: Source of Autogenerated Feature Names

## Summary

The circuit tracer ([`decoderesearch/circuit-tracer`](https://github.com/decoderesearch/circuit-tracer)) calls its feature labels **"clerps"**. Each node in the attribution graph has a `clerp` field that gives it a human-readable name. For cross-layer transcoder feature nodes the autogenerated name comes from **Neuronpedia's auto-interpretation API**, not from the circuit-tracer library itself.

---

## How Feature Names Flow into the UI

The frontend computes a final display label called `ppClerp` (preprocessed clerp). It is resolved with this priority order (highest wins):

```
ppClerp = localClerp  ||  remoteClerp  ||  clerp
```

| Source | What it is | Where it comes from |
|--------|-----------|---------------------|
| `localClerp` | User-edited annotation | Browser `localStorage` (key `local-clerp-{scan}`) |
| `remoteClerp` | LLM-autogenerated name | Neuronpedia API (see below) |
| `clerp` | Base name stored in the graph JSON | Python `graph_models.py` / JS defaults |

Source: `circuit_tracer/frontend/assets/attribution_graph/util-cg.js`, line 127.

---

## Where `clerp` Values Are Set in the Graph JSON

The Python class `Node` in `circuit_tracer/frontend/graph_models.py` sets:

| Node type | `clerp` value set in Python |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| `cross layer transcoder` | `""` (empty — populated later by Neuronpedia or user) |
| `logit` | `'Output "{token}" (p={prob:.3f})'` |
| `mlp reconstruction error` | `""` (filled in JS: `Err: mlp "{token}"`) |
| `embedding` | `""` (filled in JS: `Emb: "{token}"`) |

So for the interesting case — **transcoder feature nodes** — the `clerp` field is blank when the graph JSON is first written by `create_graph_files()`.

---

## Where Autogenerated Names Come From

### On Neuronpedia (the hosted platform)

When a graph is viewed on [Neuronpedia](https://www.neuronpedia.org), the platform's backend:

1. Looks up each feature index in its database.
2. Returns LLM-generated interpretations (auto-interp) as `remoteClerp` values via its API.
3. The frontend merges these into `ppClerp` so every feature node shows a meaningful name.

The `deDupHClerps` function in `util-cg.js` is the hook that loads remote clerps. In the open-source local server the remote list is **hardcoded empty**:

```js
// circuit_tracer/frontend/assets/attribution_graph/util-cg.js, line 64
const remoteClerps = []
```

This means **autogenerated names are only available when running on the Neuronpedia platform**, not in the self-hosted `circuit-tracer` local server.

### Fallback: HuggingFace feature data

For each feature node the frontend can also load an activation-example data file from HuggingFace:

```js
// circuit_tracer/frontend/assets/feature_examples/init-feature-examples.js
function hfUrl(scan, path) {
    const [repoId, rest] = scan.split('//')
    ...
    return `https://huggingface.co/${repoId}/resolve/main/${prefix}features/${path}`
}
```

These files (stored as binary chunks indexed by `index.json.gz`) contain top/bottom logits and activation histograms, but **not** the human-readable clerp name. The name must come from Neuronpedia or a user annotation.

### URL parameter persistence

After a user manually annotates a clerp, the value is stored in `localStorage` and also serialized into the `?clerps=…` URL parameter and into `qParams.clerps` when the graph is saved. On subsequent loads these values are restored as `localClerp`.

---

## Data-Flow Diagram

```
graph.json (output of create_graph_files.py)
│   clerp = ""  (feature nodes)
│   clerp = 'Output "X" (p=0.42)'  (logit nodes)
│
├── Neuronpedia backend
│       └── remoteClerp = "<LLM-generated name>"   ← autogenerated here
│
├── localStorage / URL ?clerps=
│       └── localClerp = "<user annotation>"
│
└── ppClerp = localClerp || remoteClerp || clerp    ← shown in UI
```

---

## Key Files (in `decoderesearch/circuit-tracer`)

| File | Relevance |
|------|-----------|
| `circuit_tracer/frontend/graph_models.py` | `Node.clerp` field definition; defaults to `""` for feature nodes |
| `circuit_tracer/utils/create_graph_files.py` | Writes `{slug}.json`; clerp stays empty for feature nodes |
| `circuit_tracer/frontend/assets/attribution_graph/util-cg.js` | `deDupHClerps()` (loads remote clerps); `hClerpUpdateFn()` (applies priority logic); `ppClerp` assignment |
| `circuit_tracer/frontend/assets/feature_examples/init-feature-examples.js` | Fetches per-feature activation data from HuggingFace (does **not** contain clerp names) |
| `circuit_tracer/frontend/assets/attribution_graph/init-cg.js` | Loads `?clerps=` URL param into `visState.clerps` |

---

## Conclusion

The **autogenerated feature names** seen in the circuit tracer attribution-graph UI are produced by Neuronpedia's **auto-interpretation pipeline** (an LLM that reads a feature's top-activating examples and writes a short description). They are served as `remoteClerp` values through Neuronpedia's API. The open-source `circuit-tracer` local server stubs this out with an empty array, so locally-run graphs show blank labels until a user manually annotates them.
